title_en: Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Trial of Disputes over Compensation for Oil Pollution Damage from Ships

articles.content_en: Article 1: Where a ship causes an oil pollution accident, causing oil pollution damage to the territory of the People's Republic of China and other sea areas under its jurisdiction, or forming a threat of oil pollution damage, the People's Court shall apply these Provisions in hearing relevant cases of disputes over compensation for ship-source oil pollution damage.

Article 2: Where a party institutes prosecution for oil pollution damage caused by persistent oil loaded in an oil tanker, or applies for establishment of a limitation fund for liability for oil pollution damage, the maritime court at the place where the ship-source oil pollution accident occurred shall have jurisdiction.
Where a ship-source oil pollution accident caused by persistent oil loaded in an oil tanker occurs outside the territory of the People's Republic of China and other sea areas under its jurisdiction, and causes oil pollution damage to the territory of the People's Republic of China and other sea areas under its jurisdiction, or forms a threat of oil pollution damage, and a party institutes prosecution for the damage caused by the ship-source oil pollution accident or applies for establishment of a limitation fund for liability for oil pollution damage, the maritime court at the place where the oil pollution damage results or at the place where preventive measures against oil pollution were taken shall have jurisdiction.

Article 3: Where oil pollution damage is caused by oil leaking from two or more ships, and the person suffering damage requests the shipowners of each leaking ship to bear compensation liability, if the damage respectively caused by each ship can be reasonably separated on the basis of factors such as the quantity of oil leaked and the harmfulness of the leaking oil to the environment, the shipowners of each leaking ship shall bear liability separately; if the damage cannot be reasonably separated, the shipowners of all leaking ships shall bear joint and several liability. However, this shall not apply where the shipowner of a leaking ship is exempted from liability according to law.
Where the shipowners of the leaking ships bear joint and several liability to the person suffering damage, the amount of compensation among themselves shall be determined according to their respective degrees of liability; if the degrees of liability are difficult to determine, they shall bear compensation liability equally. A shipowner of a leaking ship that pays an amount exceeding the amount it should compensate shall have the right to seek recourse against the other shipowners of leaking ships.

Article 4: Where oil pollution damage is caused by oil leakage resulting from a collision in which the ships are mutually at fault, the person suffering damage may request the shipowner of the leaking ship to bear all compensation liability.

Article 5: Where oil pollution damage is caused by persistent oil loaded in an oil tanker, the limitation of compensation liability shall be determined in accordance with the provisions of the Regulations on the Prevention and Control of Marine Environment Pollution by Ships and the International Convention on Civil Liability for Oil Pollution Damage, 1992.
Where oil pollution damage is caused by non-persistent fuel oil loaded in an oil tanker or by fuel oil loaded in a non-oil-tanker, the limitation of compensation liability shall be determined in accordance with the provisions of the Maritime Code on limitation of liability for maritime claims.

Article 6: Where it is proved that the oil pollution damage was caused by the shipowner's intentional act or omission, or by a reckless act or omission of the shipowner with knowledge that such damage would probably result, and the shipowner claims limitation of compensation liability, the People's Court shall not support the claim.

Article 7: Where the oil pollution damage is caused intentionally by the shipowner, and the person suffering damage requests the liability insurer or financial guarantor for ship-source oil pollution damage to pay compensation, the People's Court shall not support the request.

Article 8: Where the person suffering damage directly institutes prosecution against the liability insurer or financial guarantor for ship-source oil pollution damage, the liability insurer or financial guarantor may assert against the person suffering damage the defenses of the shipowner.
Except where the oil pollution damage is caused intentionally by the shipowner, if the liability insurer or financial guarantor asserts against the person suffering damage the defenses that it may assert against the shipowner, the People's Court shall not support such assertion.

Article 10: In determining the expenses for preventive measures and the further loss or damage caused by preventive measures, the People's Court shall reasonably determine them by taking into account factors such as the scope of pollution, the degree of pollution, the quantity of oil leaked, the reasonableness of the preventive measures, the expenses of personnel involved in oil removal and equipment put into use.

Article 11: Where anti-pollution measures are taken on a ship in distress, and the main purpose at the beginning of the operation was solely to prevent or mitigate oil pollution damage, the expenses incurred shall be determined as expenses for preventive measures.
Where the operation has the dual purpose of salvaging the ship in distress and other property and preventing or mitigating oil pollution damage, the expenses for preventive measures and the expenses for salvage measures shall be reasonably divided according to the primary and secondary ratio of the purposes; where there is no reasonable basis to distinguish the primary and secondary purposes, the relevant expenses shall be apportioned equally. However, expenses incurred after the pollution danger has been eliminated shall not be listed as expenses for preventive measures.

Article 12: Where oil leaking from a ship pollutes other ships, fishing gear, aquaculture facilities, and other property, and the person suffering damage requests the person liable for oil pollution to compensate the reasonable expenses paid for cleaning and repairing the polluted property, the People's Court shall support the request.
Where the polluted property cannot be cleaned or repaired, or the cost of cleaning or repairing exceeds its value, and the person suffering damage requests the person liable for oil pollution to compensate reasonable replacement expenses, the People's Court shall support the request, but a reasonable deduction shall be made by reference to the ratio of the actual service life of the polluted property to its expected service life.

Article 13: Where the person suffering damage is unable to carry out normal production and business operations due to ship-source oil pollution of its property, the loss of income shall be calculated on the basis of the reasonable period required for cleaning, repairing, or replacing the property.

Article 15: Where the person suffering damage engages in marine aquaculture or marine fishing without permission from the relevant competent administrative department and claims loss of income, the People's Court shall not support the claim; however, if the person requests compensation for reasonable expenses for cleaning, repairing, or replacing aquaculture or fishing facilities, the People's Court shall support the request.

Article 16: Where the person suffering damage claims loss of income caused by pollution of its property or environmental pollution, the loss shall be calculated by deducting the actual net income during the damaged period from the average net income for the same period of the preceding three years, and shall be reasonably determined with due consideration of other relevant factors affecting income.
Where the loss of income cannot be determined in accordance with the preceding paragraph, it may be reasonably determined by reference to relevant statistical data and information of government departments, or the average income of similar producers and operators in the same region during the same period.
Where the person suffering damage takes reasonable measures to avoid loss of income and requests compensation for the expenses of the reasonable measures, the People's Court shall support the request, but only to the extent of the amount of loss of income avoided.

Article 17: Where a ship-source oil pollution accident causes environmental damage, compensation for environmental damage shall be limited to the expenses of reasonable restoration measures that have actually been taken or are to be taken. The expenses of restoration measures include reasonable monitoring, assessment, and research expenses.

Article 18: Where a ship has obtained effective civil liability insurance for oil pollution damage or has corresponding financial security, if a person suffering oil pollution damage claims a maritime lien, the People's Court shall not support the claim.

Article 19: For a claim for compensation for oil pollution damage caused by non-persistent fuel oil loaded in an oil tanker or fuel oil loaded in a non-oil-tanker, the provisions of the Maritime Code on limitation of liability for maritime claims shall apply.
Where the same maritime accident causes the oil pollution damage specified in the preceding paragraph and other damage for which liability may be limited as provided in Article 207 of the Maritime Code, if the shipowner claims, in accordance with the provisions of Chapter XI of the Maritime Code, to limit its liability within the same limitation amount, the People's Court shall support the claim.

Article 20: Where measures are taken to refloat, remove, or render harmless a sunken, stranded, or distressed ship in order to avoid oil pollution damage caused by non-persistent fuel oil loaded in an oil tanker or fuel oil loaded in a non-oil-tanker, and the shipowner claims limitation of liability for the expenses incurred thereby in accordance with the provisions of Chapter XI of the Maritime Code, the People's Court shall not support the claim.

Article 21: For oil pollution damage caused by persistent oil loaded in an oil tanker, the shipowner, or the liability insurer or financial guarantor for ship-source oil pollution damage, that claims limitation of liability shall establish a limitation fund for liability for oil pollution damage.
Where the limitation fund for liability for oil pollution damage is established in cash, the amount of the fund shall be the limitation of compensation liability provided in the Regulations on the Prevention and Control of Marine Environment Pollution by Ships and the International Convention on Civil Liability for Oil Pollution Damage, 1992. Where the fund is established by way of security, the amount of the security shall be the amount of the fund plus interest during the period of establishment of the fund.

Article 22: Where the shipowner, or the liability insurer or financial guarantor for ship-source oil pollution damage, applies to establish a limitation fund for liability for oil pollution damage, and an interested party objects to the shipowner's claim for limitation of compensation liability, the objection shall be raised in writing within the objection period provided in Article 106, Paragraph 1 of the Special Maritime Procedure Law; however, raising such objection shall not affect the establishment of the fund.

Article 23: For oil pollution damage caused by persistent oil loaded in an oil tanker, where an interested party does not raise an objection within the objection period to the shipowner's claim for limitation of compensation liability, after the limitation fund for liability for oil pollution damage is established, the maritime court shall lift the preservation measures taken against the shipowner's property or return the security provided for lifting the preservation measures.

Article 24: For oil pollution damage caused by persistent oil loaded in an oil tanker, where an interested party raises an objection within the objection period to the shipowner's claim for limitation of compensation liability, after the ruling determining that the shipowner has the right to limit compensation liability takes effect, the People's Court shall lift the preservation measures taken against the shipowner's property or return the security provided for lifting the preservation measures.

Article 25: For oil pollution damage caused by persistent oil loaded in an oil tanker, where the person suffering damage, when instituting prosecution, claims that the shipowner is not entitled to limit compensation liability, the maritime court may first hear and render judgment on the dispute as to whether the shipowner is entitled to limit compensation liability.

Article 26: For oil pollution damage caused by persistent oil loaded in an oil tanker, where the person suffering damage fails to apply for registration of a claim within the prescribed period for claim registration, it shall be deemed to have waived the right to be compensated from the limitation fund for liability for oil pollution damage.

Article 27: Where the limitation fund for liability for oil pollution damage is insufficient to satisfy the relevant oil pollution damage, the fund shall be distributed proportionally according to law on the basis of the confirmed amounts of compensation.

Article 28: For oil pollution damage caused by persistent oil loaded in an oil tanker, where the shipowner, or the liability insurer or financial guarantor for ship-source oil pollution damage, applies for establishment of a limitation fund for liability for oil pollution damage, or the person suffering damage applies for registration of claims and compensation, matters not provided for in these Provisions shall be governed by the Special Maritime Procedure Law and relevant judicial interpretations.

Article 29: Before the distribution of the limitation fund for liability for oil pollution damage, where the shipowner, or the liability insurer or financial guarantor for ship-source oil pollution damage, has already compensated the oil pollution damage in advance, it may apply in writing for subrogated compensation from the fund. The subrogated compensation shall be limited to the scope of the compensation paid and shall not exceed the amount of compensation that the person receiving compensation is entitled to obtain according to law.
After accepting the application for subrogated compensation, the maritime court shall notify in writing all interested parties who have made claims against the limitation fund for liability for oil pollution damage. If an interested party has an objection to the applicant's right to claim subrogated compensation, it shall raise the objection in writing within fifteen days from the date of receipt of the notice.
After examination, if the maritime court determines that the applicant's right to subrogated compensation is established, it shall rule to confirm the right; if the applicant's claim to subrogated compensation lacks factual or legal basis, it shall rule to reject the application. If a party is dissatisfied with the ruling, it may file an appeal within ten days from the date of receipt of the written ruling.

Article 30: Where the shipowner, for the purpose of actively preventing or mitigating oil pollution damage, pays reasonable expenses or makes reasonable sacrifices, and requests to participate in the distribution of the limitation fund for liability for oil pollution damage, the People's Court shall support the request, and the matter shall be handled by reference to the provisions of Article 29, Paragraphs 2 and 3 of these Provisions.

Article 31: The meanings of the following terms in these Provisions are:
(1) 'Ship' means a seagoing vessel and other offshore mobile installations not used for military or government purposes, including oil tankers and non-oil-tankers navigating on international routes and domestic routes. Among them, an oil tanker means a ship constructed or converted for the carriage of persistent oil cargo in bulk, and any other ship actually carrying persistent oil cargo in bulk.
(2) 'Oil' means hydrocarbon mineral oils and residues thereof, limited to persistent oil cargo loaded on a ship as cargo for transport, and persistent and non-persistent fuel oil loaded for the operation of the ship itself, excluding non-persistent oil cargo loaded on a ship as cargo for transport.
(3) 'Ship-source oil pollution accident' means one or a series of events in which oil leaks from a ship and causes oil pollution damage, or, although no oil leaks, a serious and imminent threat of oil pollution damage is formed. Where a series of events arise from the same cause, they shall be regarded as one accident.
(4) 'Liability insurer or financial guarantor for ship-source oil pollution damage' means the oil pollution liability insurer or financial guarantor of the ship side that leaks oil or directly forms a threat of oil pollution damage in a maritime accident.
(5) 'Limitation fund for liability for oil pollution damage' means the compensation liability limitation fund applied for and established by the shipowner, or the liability insurer or financial guarantor for ship-source oil pollution damage, for oil pollution damage caused by persistent oil loaded in an oil tanker.

Article 32: Where judicial interpretations issued by this Court before these Provisions come into force are inconsistent with these Provisions, these Provisions shall prevail.
For cases that have already been finally adjudicated before these Provisions come into force, these Provisions shall not apply when the People's Court conducts a retrial.
